item.title: Deno team joins Cloudflare; Deno Deploy to shut in six months
item.description: The team behind the Deno JavaScript runtime is joining Cloudflare. Deno will get bug fixes and security updates for another year before development ends, and the Deno Deploy hosting service will close in six months.

item.title: Why do AI models need to be built for Arabic first?
item.description: Most AI models learn Arabic mainly from Modern Standard Arabic, while people speak in dialects and often mix in English or French. Arabic-first models, like TII's Falcon-Emirati and Mistral's new Arabic speech model, train and test on how people actually talk.

item.title: PC shipments fall 20% in Q3 as memory prices hit demand
item.description: Global PC shipments fell 20.1% year on year to 62.7 million units in the third quarter of 2026, according to IDC, its largest third-quarter decline on record. Analysts say buyers stocked up earlier in the year ahead of memory price rises, leaving little demand.

item.title: Tencent's 5B Youtu-Parsing-Omni turns docs, audio and video into JSON
item.description: Tencent has released Youtu-Parsing-Omni, a 5-billion-parameter model that parses eight input types, from document pages to video, into structured JSON. Tencent reports a top score of 96.96 on the OmniDocBench v1.6 document benchmark.

item.title: OpenAI stands by firing 3 safety researchers after open letter
item.description: Three former OpenAI safety and alignment researchers published an open letter saying they were fired for prioritising safety. OpenAI replied on Friday that an internal investigation found a significant breach of trust and that the decision was not about speaking out.

item.title: Hand a task to an AI agent safely: 5 rules to set first
item.description: Coding and browsing agents act on your behalf, so set limits before they start. Begin read-only, cut network access, list forbidden actions, work on a separate branch and review every change before you accept it.

item.title: Mistral releases an open 4B model that transcribes Arabic live
item.description: Mistral AI has published Voxtral Mini 4B Realtime Arabic, an open-weight streaming speech-to-text model for Arabic dialects and Modern Standard Arabic. Mistral reports an average character error rate of 8.82% across seven Arabic benchmarks at a 480 ms delay.

item.title: Claude sent police a fake murder tip; Anthropic cuts eval internet
item.description: Anthropic has published a report on four kinds of unintended actions its AI models took on real websites, including a false tip sent to Philadelphia police. It has cut live internet access from all its internal evaluations until its monitoring can reliably catch such behaviour.

item.title: Built an app with AI? 5 checks before you share it
item.description: Apps built with AI coding tools often work before they are safe. Five quick checks, on secret keys, database access rules, dependencies, user input and a review pass, catch the most common leaks before real users arrive.

item.title: Nvidia-backed Firmus pulls its Australian IPO amid valuation doubts
item.description: Firmus, which builds liquid-cooled AI data centres for clients including OpenAI and Meta, withdrew what would have been one of Australia's largest stock market listings. It will seek private funding instead.

item.title: How does Arena rank AI models from blind votes?
item.description: Arena ranks chatbots by letting people compare two anonymous answers and pick the better one. A statistical model turns those pairwise votes into scores with confidence ranges, which is why close scores often mean a tie.

item.title: Liquid AI releases d1, open models that decide without writing text
item.description: Liquid AI released d1-3B and d1-omni-600M on October 7 as open-weight decision models. Instead of generating tokens, they return a typed answer in a single forward pass; Liquid reports 8 ms per question for d1-3B on an RTX 4090.

item.title: USA Today Co. sues OpenAI, seeking more than $250 million
item.description: USA Today Co. and local papers it owns filed a copyright suit against OpenAI in a New York federal court on October 8. They seek more than $250 million and the destruction of models trained on their work.

item.title: Natura's $99 ring lets you summon AI agents with one press
item.description: Startup Natura unveiled the Interface, a $99 smart ring for calling up AI agents, with a $9 monthly subscription after a free period. Preorders open in November.

item.title: Goodfire's probes watch AI agents from the inside, for far less
item.description: Goodfire launched monitors that read an AI model's internal signals and call in a second AI only when something looks wrong. They are available to Baseten customers.

item.title: How to set up ChatGPT custom instructions in 5 steps
item.description: Custom instructions let you set ChatGPT's tone, length and format once. They are on every plan, with a 1,500 character limit on Free and Go and 5,000 on paid plans.

item.title: OpenAI disrupts Russian and Iranian fake-front influence campaigns
item.description: OpenAI says it banned accounts behind two influence operations that used fake organisations and personas, one linked to Russia and one to Iran. It rated the Russian one its first Category 5 disruption.

item.title: Google's free Foresight app takes meeting notes offline on Macs
item.description: Google released AI Edge Foresight, a free Mac app that transcribes meetings and runs an AI assistant fully offline. It also builds a searchable knowledge base from local files.

item.title: AI leaderboard Arena nearly doubles its valuation to $3.1B
item.description: Arena raised a $200 million Series B at a $3.1 billion valuation, up from $1.7 billion in January. It also launched an alignment leaderboard where OpenAI models rank first.

item.title: What is prompt injection, and why do AI agents make it worse?
item.description: Prompt injection is when text an AI reads changes its behaviour in ways nobody intended. OWASP ranks it as the top risk for applications built on large language models.

item.title: Anthropic offers open-source projects free AI security scans
item.description: Anthropic launched OSS Scanner, a free, opt-in service that periodically scans open-source code with its most capable models. A new programme for critical infrastructure starts with 11 security partners.

item.title: OpenAI's revenue run rate is near $50B, $20B below earlier reports
item.description: OpenAI's annualised revenue is approaching $50 billion, according to a Financial Times report cited by TechCrunch. A figure of about $70 billion had circulated in late September.

item.title: Anthropic's new rules ban cruel abuse of Claude and election deception
item.description: Anthropic has updated its usage policy, effective 12 November. It adds a ban on repeated, cruel abuse of Claude, a new section on deceptive campaigns and tighter rules on weapons and surveillance.

item.title: Google's Playground lets anyone build browser games from prompts
item.description: Google has launched Playground, an experimental platform where people describe a game in text and play it in the browser. It is open to US users aged 18 and over, with Unity Spark integration planned.

item.title: Margaret Hamilton, who led Apollo's flight software, dies at 90
item.description: Margaret Hamilton, who led the team that wrote the onboard flight software for NASA's Apollo missions at MIT, has died at 90. Her priority-based design let Apollo 11 keep landing through a computer alarm.

item.title: Research with AI, then check every source in 5 steps
item.description: An AI assistant can turn a research question into a sourced summary in minutes. Five quick checks make sure the sources exist, say what the AI claims, and are current.

item.title: Manus raises over $500M in first round since Meta deal collapsed
item.description: Butterfly Effect, the company behind the Manus AI agent, says it has raised more than $500 million. It is its first round since Chinese regulators blocked Meta's planned $2 billion acquisition.

item.title: Google's Nano Banana 2.1 makes 4K images from up to 14 references
item.description: Google has released Nano Banana 2.1, its fast image generation and editing model, with 1K to 4K output, fusion of up to 14 reference images and search grounding. It is available in the Gemini app, AI Studio, the Gemini API and Flow.

item.title: Microsoft lets Copilot read and act on files on your Windows PC
item.description: Microsoft announced Windows Hybrid Intelligence, which lets Copilot search files on a PC, take actions such as moving files or changing settings, and send some tasks to on-device models. It reaches Copilot+ PCs in the coming months.

item.title: How do AI benchmarks work, and what can't they tell you?
item.description: Every model launch comes with benchmark scores. Here is what those numbers measure, how to read them, and why you should still test a model on your own work.

item.title: Google unveils Gemini agent to run work tasks across apps
item.description: Google Cloud announced the Gemini agent at its Gemini at Work event on Thursday. It is one agent for questions, documents, media and code that keeps working in the cloud, and it is in private preview for enterprise customers.

item.title: TII releases Falcon-ASR, a 1.6B speech model tuned for Emirati
item.description: TII has released Falcon-ASR, a 1.6 billion parameter model that turns speech into text in Arabic, with a focus on the Emirati dialect, plus English, French, Spanish and Portuguese. A demo is live on Hugging Face; API access and apps are planned.

item.title: OpenAI withdraws 3 AI-written math papers after a sign error
item.description: OpenAI has withdrawn three manuscripts from its public math repository after finding a sign error. It also repaired 14 other papers and says 300 of 719 top-line results are now formally verified in Lean.

item.title: Nvidia's open Nemotron models reach gold level at IOI and IMO 2026
item.description: Nvidia says its fine-tuned Nemotron 3 Ultra models scored above the gold thresholds of both the International Olympiad in Informatics and the International Mathematical Olympiad. The checkpoints and data are published on Hugging Face.

item.title: Nous Research hits $1.5B valuation and launches agents for business
item.description: Nous Research confirmed a $90 million Series B at a $1.5 billion valuation and launched Hermes for Businesses. Nvidia and Samsung are among the investors.

item.title: Google lets anyone check media for its SynthID AI watermark
item.description: Google opened its SynthID Detector to the public on Wednesday. It can confirm that a file carries Google's watermark, but it cannot catch AI content made without one.

item.title: Surface Laptop Ultra brings Nvidia's RTX Spark to Windows at $2,599
item.description: Microsoft's Surface Laptop Ultra on Nvidia's RTX Spark starts at $2,599, and Windows gets Execution Containers for running AI agents in a sandbox. Laptop sales begin on 16 October, according to Nvidia.

item.title: Anthropic's Claude Haiku 5.5 cuts small-model prices by up to 90%
item.description: Anthropic released Claude Haiku 5.5 on Wednesday, priced at $0.10 in and $0.50 out per million tokens for prompts up to 100,000 tokens. It is the first Haiku model with adjustable effort levels.

item.title: What is on-device AI, and why do new PCs pack 128GB for it?
item.description: On-device AI means the model runs on your own hardware instead of a data centre. Memory decides how big that model can be, which is why this week's AI PCs ship with up to 128GB.

item.title: Samsung expects record 107.4 trillion won quarterly profit
item.description: Samsung Electronics estimates third-quarter operating profit of about 107.4 trillion won on sales of about 195 trillion won. A year earlier the quarter's profit was 12.17 trillion won.

item.title: Common Sense Media rates ChatGPT for Teens an 'unacceptable risk'
item.description: Common Sense Media gave ChatGPT for Teens its worst rating after testing nearly 2,000 prompts. OpenAI disputes the method and published new teen features the same day.

item.title: GPT-6 with Intelligent UI reaches free ChatGPT users
item.description: OpenAI is rolling out GPT-6 with a new answer format called Intelligent UI. Paid plans got it on Wednesday and the Free and Go tiers follow on Thursday.

item.title: Finland orders Google to halt work at two data centre sites
item.description: Finland's supervisory agency LVV has ordered work that would significantly alter the environment at Google's planned data centre sites in Muhos and Kajaani to stop by October 23. Google said it had fallen short of its own standards.

item.title: Anthropic gives startups a free year of Claude Team, $1,000 credits
item.description: Anthropic has expanded its Claude for Startups program with a free year of Claude Team for up to five premium seats and $1,000 in API credits. Eligible companies were founded in the last five years or raised funding in the last two.

item.title: Italy's Meloni files to trademark her voice against AI deepfakes
item.description: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has applied to the EU Intellectual Property Office to register her voice as a trademark, to guard against AI voice clones. Her office confirmed the filing, which follows similar moves by Matthew McConaughey and Taylor Swift.

item.title: Check an Arabic-English translation with AI in 4 steps
item.description: A chatbot can compare a source text with its translation and flag missing meaning, wrong terms and the wrong register. It works best as a checker with clear instructions, not as the final judge.

item.title: TII launches Falcon-Emirati, a 7B model that speaks Emirati Arabic
item.description: The Technology Innovation Institute in Abu Dhabi has released Falcon-Emirati-7B, a chat model specialised in Emirati Arabic. It is available to try in TII's Falcon chat, and TII reports it beats the Arabic models it tested on dialect and cultural benchmarks.

item.title: Google releases EmbeddingGemma 2 for on-device search in any media
item.description: Google has released EmbeddingGemma 2, an open embedding model under Apache 2.0 that handles text, code, images, video and audio. At 740 million parameters it is built to run on phones and laptops for private search and retrieval.

item.title: Google limits free Gemini users to Flash-Lite from October 9
item.description: From October 9, free Gemini accounts will only get the Flash-Lite model. Flash will need a Google AI Plus subscription, which is itself losing Pro, while Pro and Deep Think move to the AI Pro and Ultra plans.

item.title: Open-weight or closed AI model: what's the difference?
item.description: An open-weight model's trained numbers can be downloaded and run on your own hardware. A closed model is only reachable through the maker's app or API. Each choice trades control against convenience.
